title: KCET 2026 Mathematics
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column D4 (revised key dated 10-05-2026: no changes for Mathematics)

questions.q: $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1+1\cdot2}\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1+2\cdot3}\right)+\cdots+\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1+n(n+1)}\right)=$
questions.explanation: Each term is $\tan^{-1}(k+1)-\tan^{-1}(k)$, so the sum telescopes to $\tan^{-1}(n+1)-\tan^{-1}(1)=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{n}{n+2}\right)$.

questions.q: The corner points of the feasible region determined by the system of linear constraints are $(0,10),(5,5),(15,15),(0,20)$. Let $z=px+qy$, where $p,q>0$. The relation between $p$ and $q$, so that the maximum $z$ occurs at both points $(15,15)$ and $(0,20)$ is
questions.explanation: Equal $z$ at both points: $15p+15q=0\cdot p+20q \Rightarrow 15p=5q \Rightarrow q=3p$.

questions.q: In Linear Programming Problem (LPP), the objective function $Z=ax+by$ has the same maximum value at two corner points. The number of points at which $Z_{max}$ occurs is
questions.explanation: When the maximum occurs at two corner points, it occurs at every point of the line segment joining them, giving infinitely many optimal points.

questions.q: Probability of obtaining an even prime number on each die when a pair of dice is rolled is
questions.explanation: The only even prime is 2. P(2 on each die) $=\dfrac{1}{6}\times\dfrac{1}{6}=\dfrac{1}{36}$.

questions.q: The probability that a man and his wife live after 20 years are $\dfrac{1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{1}{3}$ respectively. The probability that neither the man nor his wife live after 20 years is
questions.explanation: P(neither) $=(1-\tfrac14)(1-\tfrac13)=\tfrac34\times\tfrac23=\tfrac12$.

questions.q: Integrating factor of the differential equation $(1-x^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}-xy=1$ is
questions.explanation: Writing as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{x}{1-x^2}y=\dfrac{1}{1-x^2}$, I.F. $=e^{\int -\frac{x}{1-x^2}dx}=e^{\frac12\ln(1-x^2)}=\sqrt{1-x^2}$.

questions.q: Recent studies suggest that 12% of the world population is left handed. Depending on parents hand usage, the chances of having left handed children are as follows: A: Both parents are left handed, chances of having left handed children = 24%; B: Both parents are right handed, chances of having left handed children = 9%; C: Father left handed and mother right handed, chances of having left handed children = 17%; D: Father right handed and mother left handed, chances of having left handed children = 22%. Given $P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=P(D)=1/4$ and L denotes child is left handed. What is the probability that $P(A|L)$?
If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are acute angles such that $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha-\beta$ satisfy the equation $\tan^2\theta-4\tan\theta+1=0$, then $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are respectively
questions.explanation: Product of roots $=1 \Rightarrow \tan(\alpha+\beta)\tan(\alpha-\beta)=1 \Rightarrow (\alpha+\beta)+(\alpha-\beta)=90^\circ \Rightarrow \alpha=45^\circ$. Sum of roots $=4$ then gives $\tan\beta=1/\sqrt3 \Rightarrow \beta=30^\circ$.
Since $r\cdot r!=(r+1)!-r!$, the sum telescopes: $\sum_{r=1}^n \left[(r+1)!-r!\right]=(n+1)!-1$.

questions.q: The solution of $3x-5<2x-4$ is
questions.explanation: $3x-5<2x-4 \Rightarrow x<1$.

questions.q:
10 distinct points are taken on a circle. Then using these points
Statement I : The number of triangles that can be formed is 100
Statement II : The number of chords that can be formed is 45
Which of the following is correct?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Triangles $=\,{}^{10}C_3=120\neq100$ (Statement I false). Chords $=\,{}^{10}C_2=45$ (Statement II true).

questions.q: How many ways can you arrange all the letters and numbers in "KCET 2025" which start with K and end with 5?
questions.explanation: "KCET 2025" has 8 symbols (K,C,E,T,2,0,2,5) with the digit 2 repeated. Fixing K first and 5 last leaves 6 symbols (C,E,T,2,0,2) with one repeated pair, giving $\dfrac{6!}{2!}=360$ arrangements.

questions.q: The value of $\lim_{x\to2}\dfrac{x^3+3x^2-9x-2}{x^3-x^2-4x+4}$ is ________
questions.note: Direct computation gives 15/4 (option B): factoring (x-2) from numerator and denominator leaves (x^2+5x+1)/(x^2+x-2), which equals 15/4 at x=2; KEA's key credits 15/2.
questions.explanation: Factoring out $(x-2)$: numerator $=(x-2)(x^2+5x+1)$, denominator $=(x-2)(x^2+x-2)$. The limit is $\dfrac{2^2+5(2)+1}{2^2+2-2}=\dfrac{15}{4}$ by direct computation; KEA's key marks $\dfrac{15}{2}$ as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If we insert two numbers between $\sqrt2$ and 4 so that the resulting sequence is in G.P., then the inserted numbers in the order are
questions.explanation: With common ratio $r$, $4=\sqrt2\cdot r^3 \Rightarrow r^3=2\sqrt2 \Rightarrow r=\sqrt2$. The inserted terms are $\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2=2$ and $2\cdot\sqrt2=2\sqrt2$.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I
a) A matrix which is not a square matrix
b) A square matrix $A'=A$
c) The diagonal elements of a diagonal matrix are same
d) A matrix which is both symmetric and skew symmetric
List-II
i) Symmetric matrix
ii) Null matrix
iii) Rectangular matrix
iv) Scalar matrix
Codes:
options: a - iii, b - i, c - iv, d - ii
a - iii, b - ii, c - iv, d - i
a - i, b - ii, c - iv, d - iii
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
questions.note: The correct match is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii (option A); KEA's key credits option (3) (a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii), which misassigns 'a' and 'b'.
questions.explanation: a is a rectangular matrix (iii), b is a symmetric matrix (i), c is a scalar matrix (iv), and d (symmetric and skew-symmetric together) must be the null matrix (ii), giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii; KEA's key marks option (3) as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I : If $A$ is a non-singular matrix, then $A^{-1}$ exists.
Statement II : If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric matrices of same order, then $(AB-BA)$ is a skew symmetric matrix.
Choose the correct option.
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is false
Statement I is true and Statement II is true
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.explanation: A non-singular matrix always has an inverse (Statement I true). For symmetric $A,B$: $(AB-BA)'=B'A'-A'B'=BA-AB=-(AB-BA)$, so it is skew symmetric (Statement II true).

questions.q: A row matrix has only
options: One row with one or more columns
One column with one or more rows
questions.explanation: By definition, a row matrix has exactly one row and one or more columns.

questions.q: Let $X$ be a matrix of order $2\times n$ and $Z$ be a matrix of order $2\times p$. If $n=p$, then the order of the matrix $7X-5Z$ is:
questions.explanation: Since $n=p$, both matrices have order $2\times n$, and subtraction/addition preserves order, so $7X-5Z$ is $2\times n$.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct?
options: Determinant is a number associated to a matrix.
Determinant is a unique number associated to a square matrix.
Determinant is not defined for a square matrix.
questions.explanation: A determinant is a unique real number associated with every square matrix.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are invertible matrices of same order, then which of the following is $\underline{\text{not}}$ correct?
questions.note: Option (1) as printed is a true and standard identity, so the statement that is actually not correct is option (2) (it omits the identity matrix I, so dimensionally it cannot hold in general); KEA's key nevertheless credits option (1).
questions.explanation: $A(\text{adj }A)=(\text{adj }A)A=|A|I$ is the correct identity (option 2 wrongly omits $I$), so option (1) as printed is a true statement; KEA's key nevertheless marks option (1) as the one that is not correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are invertible square matrices of order $n$, then which of the following is $\underline{\text{not}}$ correct?
questions.explanation: In general $\det(A+B)\neq\det A+\det B$, while the other three identities always hold.

questions.q: The area of the triangle with vertices $(3,8),(-4,2)$ and $(5,1)$ is $\dfrac{P}{4}$, then the value of $P$ is
The system of equations $x+2y=3$ and $2x+3y=3$ has
questions.explanation: Determinant of coefficients $=1(3)-2(2)=-1\neq0$, so the system has a unique solution.

questions.q: If $\vec a=2\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k, \vec b=\alpha\hat i+\beta\hat j+2\hat k$ and $|\vec a+\vec b|=|\vec a-\vec b|$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $|\vec a+\vec b|=|\vec a-\vec b|\Rightarrow \vec a\cdot\vec b=0\Rightarrow 2\alpha+2\beta-2=0\Rightarrow \alpha+\beta=1$.

questions.q: If $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k, \vec b=\hat j-\hat k$ and $\vec a\times\vec c=\vec b, \vec a\cdot\vec c=3$, then $\vec c$ is
questions.explanation: Let $\vec c=(x,y,z)$. $\vec a\times\vec c=(z-y,x-z,y-x)=(0,1,-1)$ gives $z=y,\ x-z=1$. With $x+y+z=3$: $3y+1=3\Rightarrow y=\tfrac23$, so $x=\tfrac53,z=\tfrac23$, i.e. $\vec c=\tfrac53\hat i+\tfrac23\hat j+\tfrac23\hat k$.

questions.q: The value of $\lambda$ for which the vectors $\vec a=2\hat i+\lambda\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$ are orthogonal is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\cdot\vec b=2+2\lambda+3=0\Rightarrow \lambda=-\dfrac52$.

questions.q: The angle between the lines whose direction ratios are $a,b,c$ and $b-c,c-a,a-b$ is
questions.explanation: Dot product $=a(b-c)+b(c-a)+c(a-b)=0$, so the lines are perpendicular, i.e. angle $=90^\circ$.

questions.q: The measure of the angle between the lines $x=k-1,y=2k+1,z=2k+3, k\in\mathbb R$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-1}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Direction ratios are $(1,2,2)$ and $(2,1,2)$. $\cos\theta=\dfrac{1(2)+2(1)+2(2)}{3\times3}=\dfrac89$.

questions.q: The line $L_1$ joining the two points $(-1,2)$ and $(3,6)$ divides the line $L_2$ which passes through $(3,-1)$ in the ratio 1:3 internally, then the equation of $L_2$ is
questions.explanation: The point dividing $(-1,2)$ and $(3,6)$ in ratio 1:3 is $\left(\dfrac{3-3}{4},\dfrac{6+6}{4}\right)=(0,3)$. $L_2$ through $(3,-1)$ and $(0,3)$ has slope $-\dfrac43$, giving $4x+3y-9=0$.

questions.q:
In the figure
Statement I : When $\alpha>\beta\ge0$, the section is hyperbola
Statement II : When $\beta=90^\circ$, the section is ellipse
Which of the following is correct? [Figure: a cone cut by a plane, $\alpha$ = semi-vertical angle of the cone, $\beta$ = angle the cutting plane makes with the axis]
options: Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true
questions.explanation: When $0\le\beta<\alpha$ the plane cuts both nappes giving a hyperbola (Statement I true); when $\beta=90^\circ$ the plane is perpendicular to the axis, giving a circle, not an ellipse (Statement II false).

questions.q: The three points $A(2,4,3), B(4,a,9)$ and $C(10,-1,7)$ form a right-angled triangle with $\angle B=90^\circ$, then the value of 'a' is
questions.note: Solving BA.BC=0 with the printed coordinates A(2,4,3), B(4,a,9), C(10,-1,7) gives a=4 or a=-1, which does not match any listed pair exactly; the printed coordinates are likely corrupted. KEA's key credits '-2 or 4' (option B), kept as the official answer.
questions.explanation: With $\angle B=90^\circ$, $\vec{BA}\cdot\vec{BC}=0$. Using the given points this simplifies to a quadratic in $a$; solving it gives the values of $a$ for which the triangle is right-angled at $B$ (as per KEA key: $-2$ or $4$).

questions.q: If $\lim_{x\to3}\left(\dfrac{x^2-ax-3a}{x-3}\right)=5$, then $a+b=$
questions.note: The printed limit expression (x^2-ax-3a)/(x-3) contains only the constant 'a', so 'a+b' in the question cannot be evaluated as printed; the question text is corrupted (missing a 'b' term). KEA's key credits option (3), a+b=3, kept as the official answer.
questions.explanation: For the limit to be finite as the denominator $\to0$, the numerator must vanish at $x=3$, which fixes the constant(s) in the expression so that the limit equals 5; solving as intended by KEA gives $a+b=3$ (as per KEA key; the printed expression appears to be missing a term, likely a transcription issue in the source paper).

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2-1 & \text{if } x\ge2\\x+1 & \text{if } x<2\end{cases}$, then $\lim_{x\to2^+}f(x)+\lim_{x\to2^-}f(x)=$
questions.note: Both one-sided limits equal 3 (2^2-1=3 and 2+1=3), so the sum is 6 (option C); KEA's key credits 5 (option B).
questions.explanation: $\lim_{x\to2^+}f(x)=2^2-1=3$ and $\lim_{x\to2^-}f(x)=2+1=3$, so the sum is $6$ by direct computation; KEA's key marks $5$ as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If $y=\sqrt{\tan x+y}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=$
questions.note: Implicit differentiation of y^2=tan x+y gives y'=sec^2 x/(2y-1) (option B); KEA's key credits sin^2 x/(2y-1) (option D).
questions.explanation: Squaring, $y^2=\tan x+y$. Differentiating: $2yy'=\sec^2x+y' \Rightarrow y'=\dfrac{\sec^2x}{2y-1}$ by direct computation; KEA's key marks $\dfrac{\sin^2x}{2y-1}$ as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}ax+7 & \text{if } x<1\\2x-3 & \text{if } x=1\\dfrac{x+b}{b} & \text{if } x>1\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=1$, then
questions.note: As printed, the third piece (x+b)/b requires (1+b)/b=-1, giving b=-1/2 for continuity, which matches no option; the printed third piece is likely corrupted. KEA's key credits a=-8, b=2 (option D), kept as the official answer.
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the left-hand limit to equal $f(1)$: $a+7=2(1)-3=-1\Rightarrow a=-8$. Matching the right-hand branch with $f(1)=-1$ fixes $b$ as per KEA's key, giving $a=-8,b=2$ (as per KEA key; the printed right-hand expression may contain a transcription error).

questions.q: The second order derivative of $\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2x^2-1}\right)$ with respect to $\cos^{-1}(2x^2-1)$, where $0<x<\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\sec^{-1}(1/y)=\cos^{-1}(y)$, we get $\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2x^2-1}\right)=\cos^{-1}(2x^2-1)$, i.e. the two quantities are identical. So $u=v$, hence $\dfrac{d^2u}{dv^2}=0$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$, then $f'\left(\dfrac12\right)=$
questions.note: For |x|<=1, sin^{-1}(2x/(1+x^2))=2 tan^{-1}x, so f'(1/2)=2/(1+0.25)=8/5 (option B); KEA's key credits 4/5 (option A).
questions.explanation: For $|x|\le1$, $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$, so $f'(x)=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$, giving $f'(1/2)=\dfrac{2}{1.25}=\dfrac85$ by direct computation; KEA's key marks $\dfrac45$ as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If $\sqrt x\,\sqrt[3]{y}=(x+y)^n$ and $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y=0$, then $n=$
questions.explanation: Taking logs: $\tfrac12\ln x+\tfrac13\ln y=n\ln(x+y)$. Differentiating and using $xy'=y$ (i.e. $y'=y/x$) simplifies the equation to $\dfrac{5}{6x}=\dfrac{n}{x}$, giving $n=\dfrac56$.

questions.q: In a Mahakumbh, a drone camera is moving along $3y=x^3-3$. When y-coordinate changes 9 times as fast as x-coordinate, it captures good quality pictures. Then one of the precise positions of the drone at that instant is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^2=9\Rightarrow x=\pm3$. At $x=3$: $3y=27-3=24\Rightarrow y=8$, giving the point $(3,8)$.

questions.q: A Youtube short video is getting viral according to $f(t)=-2t^3+3t^2+5$. At what time does the video get maximum number of shares? (t is in hours)
questions.explanation: $f'(t)=-6t^2+6t=6t(1-t)=0\Rightarrow t=0,1$. $f''(t)=-12t+6$; at $t=1$, $f''=-6<0$, so maximum occurs at $t=1$.

questions.q: $\int xf(x)dx+\dfrac{f(x)}{2}=0$, then $f(x)$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Differentiating the given relation, $xf(x)+\tfrac12f'(x)=0\Rightarrow \dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}=-2x\Rightarrow \ln f(x)=-x^2+C\Rightarrow f(x)=Ce^{-x^2}$.

questions.q: One of the possible functions $f(x)$ which satisfies $\int_{-2}^2 f(x)dx=0$ is
questions.explanation: $f(x)=\log\left(\frac{2+x}{2-x}\right)$ is an odd function since $f(-x)=-f(x)$, so its integral over the symmetric interval $[-2,2]$ is zero.

questions.q: $\int_{a-6}^{b-6}f(x+6)dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Substituting $u=x+6$, the limits become $a$ to $b$, giving $\int_a^b f(u)du=\int_a^b f(x)dx$.

questions.q: If 'n' is a natural number, then $\int \dfrac{\sin^n x}{\cos^{n+2}x}dx=$
questions.explanation: $\int \tan^n x\sec^2x\,dx=\dfrac{\tan^{n+1}x}{n+1}+C$ by the substitution $t=\tan x$.

questions.q: $\int e^{-x\log 2}2^x dx=$
questions.explanation: $e^{-x\log2}=2^{-x}$, so the integrand is $2^{-x}\cdot2^x=1$, and $\int 1\,dx=x+C$.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y^2=x^3$, the y-axis and the lines $y=1$ and $y=8$ is
questions.explanation: $x=y^{2/3}$, so Area $=\int_1^8 y^{2/3}dy=\left[\dfrac{3}{5}y^{5/3}\right]_1^8=\dfrac35(32-1)=\dfrac{93}{5}$ sq. units.

questions.q: The area enclosed by the curve $x=\sqrt3\cos\theta, y=\sqrt3\sin\theta$ is
questions.explanation: This is a circle of radius $\sqrt3$, so its area is $\pi(\sqrt3)^2=3\pi$ sq. units.

questions.q: Sum of the squares of the order and degree (if defined) of a differential equation $2y'+(y'')^2=\sqrt{y''-3}$ is
questions.explanation: The order is 2 (from $y''$). Squaring to remove the radical makes $(y'')^4$ the highest power, so the degree is 4. Sum of squares $=2^2+4^2=4+16=20$.

questions.q: If $A=\{a,b,c,d,e,f\}$, then the number of subsets of A which contains at least 2 elements is
questions.explanation: Total subsets $=2^6=64$. Removing the empty set (1) and singletons (6) leaves $64-1-6=57$.

questions.q: If $A=\{1,2,3,4,\ldots,10\}$, then the number of non empty subsets of A containing only even number is
questions.explanation: The even numbers in $A$ are $\{2,4,6,8,10\}$ (5 elements), giving $2^5-1=31$ non-empty subsets.

questions.q: The domain of the function $\sqrt{\dfrac{x-7}{9-x}}$ is
questions.explanation: We need $\dfrac{x-7}{9-x}\ge0$ with $x\neq9$. This holds for $7\le x<9$, i.e. the domain is $[7,9)$.

questions.q: If $n(A)=2$ and the number of relations from set A to set B is 1024, then $n(B)$ is
questions.explanation: Number of relations $=2^{n(A)\cdot n(B)}=2^{2n(B)}=1024=2^{10}\Rightarrow 2n(B)=10\Rightarrow n(B)=5$.

questions.q: Probability of at least one of the events A and B occur is 0.6. If A and B occur simultaneously with probability 0.2, then $P(\bar A)+P(\bar B)$ is
questions.explanation: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)\Rightarrow 0.6=P(A)+P(B)-0.2\Rightarrow P(A)+P(B)=0.8$. So $P(\bar A)+P(\bar B)=2-0.8=1.2$.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\sin(x+\pi/6)+\cos(x+\pi/6)$ is attained at $x=$
questions.explanation: $\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\sqrt2\sin(\theta+\pi/4)$ is maximum when $\theta+\pi/4=\pi/2$, i.e. $x+\pi/6+\pi/4=\pi/2\Rightarrow x=\pi/12$.

questions.q: The angles of a triangle are in A.P and the greatest angle is double the least angle, then sine of the third angle is
questions.explanation: Let angles be $a-d,a,a+d$; sum gives $a=60^\circ$. Greatest $=$ twice least: $a+d=2(a-d)\Rightarrow d=20^\circ$. The angles are $40^\circ,60^\circ,80^\circ$; the third (middle) angle is $60^\circ$, and $\sin60^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

questions.q: The mean and standard deviation of 100 items are 50 and 4, respectively then the sum of all squares of the items is
questions.explanation: $\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum x^2}{n}-\bar x^2 \Rightarrow \sum x^2=n(\sigma^2+\bar x^2)=100(16+2500)=251600$.

questions.q: Probability of occurrence of an event A is 1/2 and that of B is 3/10. If A and B are mutually exclusive, then the probability of occurrence of neither A nor B is
questions.explanation: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)=\tfrac12+\tfrac{3}{10}=\tfrac{8}{10}$. P(neither) $=1-\tfrac{8}{10}=\tfrac15$.

questions.q: Let R be the relation in the set N given by $R=\{(a,b):a=b-2,b>6\}$. Which of the following is the correct answer?
questions.explanation: Checking $(6,8)$: $a=6=b-2=8-2$ and $b=8>6$, so it satisfies both conditions.

questions.q: $f(x)=(x+1)^2$ for $x\ge1$. $g(x)$ is a function whose graph is the reflection of the graph of $f(x)$ in the line $y=x$, then $g(x)$ is
questions.explanation: $g$ is the inverse of $f$. From $y=(x+1)^2$ with $x\ge1$, $x+1=\sqrt y$ (positive root), so $x=\sqrt y-1$, i.e. $g(x)=\sqrt x-1$.

questions.q: If $\sin^{-1}x+\sin^{-1}y=\pi/2$, then $x^2$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\sin^{-1}x=\dfrac\pi2-\sin^{-1}y=\cos^{-1}y\Rightarrow x=\sqrt{1-y^2}\Rightarrow x^2=1-y^2$.
